name: DJI RS 4
about: Joint axes, offsets and boxes for the sandbox's Gimbal object. Lengths in mm, in the HANDLE's frame (the Gimbal object's mount): handle along z, hand end up (+z), camera end down; +y is the camera's left. All joints at 0 is the gimbal's HOME pose: the camera looks along +x (front), level, no roll. Each joint maps the RS 4's reading to the model angle as sign * reading + offset; Recalibrate sets the offsets from a reading taken in the home pose. DJI publishes no CAD or axis dimensions for the RS 4: the sizes below are estimates from its overall size (370 x 191 x 189 mm unfolded). A balanced gimbal has all three axes through the camera's centre of gravity, so 'point' is the same for each joint. Parts: the pan arm drops behind the camera (-x) to the roll motor on J2's axis; the roll arm goes round the camera's right (-y) to the tilt motor. Copy this file to make a model for another gimbal or rig; the Gimbal object picks it by file name. max_dps: the fastest each joint may turn, for the bake's speed check (DJI gives 360 deg/s as the RS 4's maximum controlled rotation speed; the sandbox's run drive turns J1 at up to 180 deg/s).

joints.name: J1
joints.about: pan motor, handle axis. Offset: the home reading J1 173.5 is 0.

joints.name: J2
joints.about: roll motor, behind the camera, along the lens at home. Offset: the home reading J2 -179.0 is 0.

joints.name: J3
joints.about: tilt motor, beside the camera (its right); +model J3 tilts the lens towards the hand end. The RS 4's J3 reading turns the other way (sign -1). Offset: the home reading J3 -69.4 is 0.

camera.about: camera centre (on all three axes when balanced) and its lens and right directions at home. No camera body is drawn: the Gimbal's Camera object sits here.
